comments.content: `valueFromLine<double>` uses `std::strtof` (float) instead of `std::strtod` (double). This truncates precision for all node coordinates and result values. Use `std::strtod`.

`readNodes` calls `points->SetPoint(nodeID, coords.data())` unconditionally, even when the line did not match `keyCodeCoord` (coords is empty). This reads out of bounds. Move the `SetPoint`/`mapNodes` update inside the `if` block.

`readElements` uses `mapNodes.at(node)` which throws `std::out_of_range` if a node id is missing. Unlike `readResults`, this is not caught, so a malformed/partial FRD file will crash. Wrap in try/catch or use `find`.

`readElements` reads `info` (type/group/material) from the `-1` line, but the `-2` node line may be processed before `info` is populated if the file order differs, and `mapCcxTypeNodes[info[0]]` will silently insert a 0 entry for unknown types, causing `topoElem.size() == 0` to never match and cells to be dropped. Validate `info[0]` against `mapCcxTypeNodes` before use.

In `readResults`, `countScaPos` is only reset inside the `-1` branch. If a `-2` continuation line appears before any `-1` line (or after a `-1` that threw), `countScaPos` is stale/uninitialized, leading to incorrect scalar/vector classification. Initialize `countScaPos = 0` before the loop and reset it in both branches as appropriate.

When `mapNodes.at(node)` throws in the `-1` branch, `nodes.emplace_back` is skipped but `countNodes` is still incremented and `vecValues`/`scaValues` may be partially filled. Subsequent `SetTuple(mapNodes.at(node), ...)` calls outside the try block will then throw uncaught. Guard the tuple-setting block with the same try/catch or track validity.

`vecArray->SetNumberOfComponents(numComps - scalarPos.size())` can be 0 when all components are scalar; VTK may warn or misbehave. The array is only added when `numComps != scalarPos.size()`, but it is still constructed and filled. Consider skipping construction when there are no vector components.

`readFRD` reuses the same `points` and `cells` objects for every grid created per (step, analysisType). Since `grid->SetPoints(points)` and `grid->SetCells(...)` share the same underlying data, later modifications or VTK pipeline updates can affect all grids. Also, `cellTypes.data()` is passed to `SetCells` which expects a `vtkUnsignedCharArray` or similar; passing a raw `int*` here is incorrect and will not compile/behave as intended. Use `vtkCellArray` directly via `SetCells(cells)`.

When `grids` is empty, `multiBlock->SetBlock(0, grid)` is called after `SetNumberOfBlocks(grids.size())` which is 0. This sets block 0 without increasing the block count, leaving the multiblock inconsistent. Call `SetNumberOfBlocks(1)` before setting the block.

`frdToVTK` opens the file but never checks `ifstr.is_open()`/`ifstr.good()` after opening. If the file cannot be opened despite `isReadable()`, `readFRD` will silently return an empty multiblock. Add a check and throw `Base::FileException` on failure.

`frdToVTK` uses `PyArg_ParseTuple` with `"et"` and `PyMem_Free`, which is correct, but the method is registered with `add_varargs_method` and does not accept keyword arguments. Consider using `Py::Tuple`/`Py::String` helpers for consistency with the rest of the file and to avoid manual memory management.
